title: How Quarto works

steps.say: Render once more and read the log. keep-md: true keeps the file Quarto makes half way, so we can look inside.
Stage 1: knitr runs every R chunk and writes plain Markdown: your text, the code, what it printed, and a link to the chart picture.
Stage 2: Pandoc turns that Markdown into HTML. With embed-resources, even the chart is packed inside, as a long line of text.
The browser shows the result. When a render fails, the log says which stage broke: an R error comes from knitr, a format error from Pandoc.
Other formats change only the last stage: the same Markdown becomes a Word file and, through Typst, a PDF.

## Summary

Unemployment **fell** in most regions between 2022 and 2025.
*Jazan* is the exception. This note shows the national
trend and the latest rates.[^1]
The data cover:

- 13 regions and the Kingdom as a whole
- 16 quarters, from 2022 Q1 to 2025 Q4

Official figures are on the [GASTAT website](https://www.stats.gov.sa).

[^1]: All figures in this note are synthetic, made for training.

## Method

The unemployment rate is

$$
u = \frac{U}{U + E} \times 100
$$

where $U$ is the number unemployed and $E$ the number employed.

## Data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
rates <- read_csv("unemployment.csv")
glimpse(rates)
```

## Trend

```{r}
kingdom <- rates |> filter(region == "Kingdom")
ggplot(kingdom, aes(date, rate)) + geom_line()
```
